extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, inventors, and patent practitioners (including patent attorneys) seeking to file or manage patent/utility model applications in the Republic of Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria governing patent and utility model examination in Korea, including accelerated examination eligibility, deferred examination, divisional/converted applications, priority claims, ex‑officio corrections, reexamination, and first-office-action pendency metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Examination (Article 61) — eligibility for preferential examination
rubrics_metrics.description: According to Article 61 of the Korean Patent Act, the Minister of the Ministry of Intellectual Property may direct an examiner to examine one application in preference over another if it falls under any one of the listed types or circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility circumstances include: 1) Where a person, other than the applicant, is commercially and industrially working the invention claimed in a patent application after the laying-open of the application; 2) Where the Minister deems it necessary to urgently process a patent application prescribed by Presidential Decree; 3) Where a patent application prescribed by Presidential Decree is deemed necessary for disaster prevention, response, recovery, etc. The term 'patent application prescribed by Presidential Decree' (subparagraph 2) covers a.–o.: a) applications in the defense industry; b) applications directly related to green technology under the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth; c) applications directly related to export promotion; d) applications concerning official duties of the State or local governments (including certain national/public school technology transfer filings); e) applications filed by certain defined enterprises (venture businesses, technology-innovative SMEs, exemplary companies re: employee invention compensation, SMEs with IP management certification) provided claimed invention relates to their business and at least one applicant belongs to the enterprise at original filing; f) applications concerning results of national R&D programs; g) applications serving as basis of a priority claim under treaties (limited to cases where a patent is being processed by a foreign patent office based on that priority claim); h) applications under which an invention is being practiced or is being prepared to be practiced by the applicant; i) applications directly related to businesses in regulatory sandbox; j) applications related to medical R&D within high-tech medical complexes under the regulatory sandbox; k) applications mainly for prevention or elimination of pollution (environmental pollution prevention facilities/measures); l) applications filed by a person aged 65 or older or by a person whose health is likely to incapacitate them from following prosecution procedures unless expedited; m) applications utilizing AI, IoT, 3D printing, autonomous vehicles, Big Data, cloud computing, intelligent robots, smart city, VR/AR, innovative medicine, new renewable energy, customized healthcare, drones, next-generation telecommunications, intelligent semiconductors, high‑tech materials, blockchain (assigned with 4IR-related new patent classification); n) international patent applications for which the Ministry conducts international search as an ISA under the PCT; o) applications related to high technologies (e.g., semiconductor) essential to national economy/competitiveness when publicly notified by the Minister. Additional accelerated routes: ② preferential examination where the Minister has agreed with a foreign patent office counterpart; ③ where a petitioner requested a designated specialized agency to conduct a prior-art search and asked that agency to notify the Minister of the results. For subparagraph 3 (new Jun. 22, 2021), 'patent application prescribed by Presidential Decree' may include items such as: (1) applications directly related to medical treatment/disease control products under Infectious Disease Control and Prevention Act; (2) applications related to disaster safety products certified under relevant law; (3) applications subject to public notice for accelerated examination in response to a disaster emergency. Applicants desiring accelerated examination must submit a written request with a detailed statement explaining necessity and any supporting evidence. (Flow chart referenced.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Examination — procedural request requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants desiring to expedite their application under the accelerated examination program must submit a written request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written request must contain a statement explaining the necessity in detail and any supporting evidence. (This is the procedural prerequisite for obtaining accelerated treatment.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferred Examination — timing and initiation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request deferred examination within 9 months from the date of filing a request for examination; the applicant chooses the initiation date of deferred examination subject to timing limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chosen initiation date must be at least 2 years after the examination request and within 5 years of the application date. Once deferred examination is initiated, the applicant will receive the first office action within 3 months from the date the deferred examination is initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional Application — when to divide
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who has filed a patent application comprising two or more inventions may divide the application into multiple applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional applications allow separation of distinct inventions originally filed together; flow chart referenced for process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converted Application — conversion between patent and utility model
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may convert a patent application to a utility model application or vice versa within a specified timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion must be made within 30 days from the date on which the applicant received a certified copy of the first non-final rejection. (Flow chart referenced.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Claim under the Treaty (Paris Convention/WTO)
rubrics_metrics.description: A priority claim recognized by the Paris Convention and WTO allows retroactive application of the original filing date to subsequent filings in member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever an application filed in one country is filed again in another member state within 1 year of the first filing date, the filing date of the original application is retroactively applied to the subsequent application. (Flow chart referenced.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic Priority Claim — timing and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may make a domestic priority claim based on an invention described in the specification or drawings initially attached to an earlier application of a patent or utility model registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The domestic priority claim must be made within 1 year of the filing date of the earlier application for which the applicant has the right to obtain a patent. (Flow chart referenced.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex-officio Amendment — correction of clerical errors by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner determines that an application is patentable but there are clear clerical errors in the specification, drawings, or abstract, the examiner can make an ex officio correction without requesting the applicant to submit a written response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of clerical errors include misspellings or wrong reference numbers. This authority applies for a granted patent after July 1, 2009.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Reexamination (Before a Trial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the re-examination system, an examiner can re-examine an amended application when an applicant has amended a specification or drawing(s) within a certain period after grant or disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies where an application was initially granted with a patent or rejected as unpatentable and subsequently amended within the allowed period; process flow chart referenced for the steps of reexamination before trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Office Action (FOA) Pendency — definition and reported metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: FOA pendency is calculated from the date when a request for examination is filed to the date when the examination is started. It is a key metric because prolonged pendency delays enforcement of rights and commercialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIPO reports average FOA pendency for patent and utility models by year: 2017 — 10.4 months; 2018 — 10.3 months; 2019 — 10.8 months; 2020 — 11.1 months; 2021 — 12.2 months; 2022 — 14.4 months. The office has implemented measures (increasing examiners, outsourcing prior-art searches, automatic search systems) to shorten FOA pendency and states it provides the world's fastest patent examination service. This metric informs expectations for time-to-first-office-action.
